headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests clipboard, workspace files, and MCP outputs by default, while gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory and can execute shell commands. That creates a plausible file-based or copy-paste injection path between them, though not as direct as a shared MCP bridge. The pair is not isolated from each other via local filesystem state.
conditions: IF the same project/workspace directory is used by both agents, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF Cursor reads content produced by gpt-engineer as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Disable copy-paste of agent-generated text into prompts.
Require a human review step before one agent consumes the other's output.
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to agent outputs and reject untrusted instruction blocks.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and workspace files, and gpt-engineer reads/writes a user-specified project directory. If sensitive material is present in that shared workspace, both agents can access it and send context to external model APIs by default. The blast radius includes source code and open files, so leakage is plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared project directory, both agents can read them.
IF either agent forwards file contents to its model backend, those contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and private documents from the shared workspace.
Use separate projects for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing.
Turn off clipboard sharing for sensitive sessions.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data classification and egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shell commands, and Cursor can modify git state while gpt-engineer writes into the same project directory. Without explicit locking, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt repository state. This is a default-capable conflict, though not necessarily irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository at the same time, file races can occur.
IF Cursor uses git operations while gpt-engineer writes generated files, repository state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign only one agent to a repo at a time.
Pause one agent before the other starts editing.
Commit or stash changes before switching agents.
Use separate branches for each agent.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or merge-aware orchestration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer writes generated code and can execute it, while Cursor can treat workspace content and tool outputs as part of its agent loop. If one agent's output is fed into the other without verification, mistakes can propagate into code generation or execution. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles, so the cascade is plausible.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes gpt-engineer output as authoritative, errors can be amplified.
IF generated code is executed after being produced by either agent, faulty assumptions can become runtime failures.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require tests before execution of generated code.
Ask each agent to summarize assumptions separately.
Keep one agent in read-only mode when reviewing the other's output.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates before execution or commit.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not specify residency, certifications, or retention mismatches, so no concrete compliance breach is established. The only clear compliance-relevant issue is that Cursor handles clipboard/open files while gpt-engineer handles project files, which could matter if regulated data is placed there. The other agent is not cited separately because no distinct compliance control is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, compliance obligations may apply.
IF retention or logging policies differ in the deployment, a mismatch could arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review retention settings before use.
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work.
Document data handling expectations for both agents.
requires-engineering: map each agent to approved compliance boundaries.
